text: Why does `public boolean equals(Point o)` fail to override anything?
choices: Point is not a subclass of Object
The method being overridden takes Object, so this is an overload and the collections call the inherited version
explanation: Chapter 12's overloading rules: a different parameter type is a different method. The result is a silent wrong-behaviour bug, which is exactly why @Override should always be written — it turns this into a compile error.
